question.text: The total open interest in a 91-day T-Bill future is Rs. 5,000 crores. What is the maximum position a trading member can hold?

explanation.text: The Logic: The 91-day T-Bill futures trading-member position limit is 15% of the total open interest or Rs. 1,000 crores, whichever is higher. With total open interest of Rs. 5,000 crores, 15% works out to Rs. 750 crores, so the higher of the two — and therefore the binding TM limit — is Rs. 1,000 crores. The Trap: Rs. 750 crores is only the 15% figure, which is not the binding limit because the rule uses "whichever is higher". Rs. 500 crores uses 10% (not in the rule) and Rs. 1,500 crores uses 30%. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-IV workbook (Dec 2025), page 235 (T-Bill position-limit table).
